display.purpose: The requested speed on the OLED; the one large number on screen.

headline.purpose: The V-Clicker wordmark beside the logo.

number-key.purpose: Legends on the number-row speed keys.

readout.purpose: Values in the OLED's three readouts.

status.purpose: OLED and indicator status line, hotkey caps, app names in the window picker.

key-legend.purpose: Legends on keycaps and the LED badge.

label.purpose: Row captions, LED-check labels, Studio field labels.

segment.purpose: Legends in segmented clusters; SemiBold on the chosen cap.

unit.purpose: Units at the right of number fields; sub-legends on amber and coral keys.

silkscreen.purpose: Uppercase, tracked group labels on the plate.

caption.purpose: Uppercase, tracked captions on the OLED (readouts, LOCK).

body-list.purpose: Lists, text fields, choice boxes, menus.

note.purpose: OLED message line, subtitles, rate hint, banner notes.

note-small.purpose: Studio help notes, window titles in the picker.

shadows.name: key-shadow
shadows.purpose: Short soft shadow of every keycap at rest (two passes: 1.5dp at alpha 90/255, inflated 1dp at 2.5dp and alpha 35/255). Removed when pressed or latched.

shadows.name: key-skirt
shadows.purpose: The skirt showing around the face: 2.5dp at the sides, 5.5dp at the front; 2.5dp at the front when pressed.

shadows.name: face-dish
shadows.purpose: Every keycap face, lighter at the top edge.

shadows.name: well-edge
shadows.purpose: Shaded 1px edge of every recess (dark above, catching light below).

shadows.name: glass-bezel
shadows.purpose: Bezel around display glass: the plate darkened 45%, shaded like a recess, 11dp radius outside, 8dp glass inside.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Focus on keys (6dp) and wells (7dp); the edge of a well being edited or listening. Ink on the amber key itself.

motion.name: instant
motion.purpose: No animation anywhere: hover, press (1.5dp travel), latch, lamps and selection repaint at once.

components.name: Start Key (Primary)
components.description: The one amber key per window: the wide Start key on the main window (Run, Confirm, Apply, OK elsewhere), hotkey as a sub-legend.

components.name: Stop Key (Coral, latched)
components.description: The Start key while clicking: coral, held down; pressing it stops. Delete uses the same coral key, unlatched.

components.name: Action Key (Mod)
components.description: Grey modifier key for actions: Macro Studio, Capture, Choose, New, Rename, Save, Record, Cancel.

components.name: Number-Row Key (Alpha)
components.description: Graphite alpha key for options and small or repeated actions; here a speed preset with its unit as a sub-legend.

components.name: Segmented Keys
components.description: Mutually exclusive options as keys in one recess; the chosen key is the light cap, held down.

components.name: Number Field
components.description: Anything typed sits in a recess; the edge turns amber while editing; the unit sits at the right.

components.name: Silkscreen Section
components.description: A group is named by uppercase tracked lettering on the plate followed by a hairline; never a card.

components.name: LED Check
components.description: An on/off option as a lock key: a small cap whose lamp lights amber when on, the label beside it.

components.name: On-screen Indicator
components.description: A sliver of display glass over the game: a pill with a status lamp and the main window's status words.

narrative.overview:
V-Clicker is drawn as a piece of hardware sitting next to the game: a graphite anodized plate, PBT keycaps in two flat layers (a face on a skirt), a black OLED module set into the plate, LEDs for anything that is on or off, and silkscreen lettering where other apps put panels. Every action is a key you press, every option is a key you hold down, every number you type sits in a recess in the plate, and every live number sits behind glass. The window is small and dense like a keyboard's top case, and it is built to be read at a glance from beside a game: running or not, how fast, what F6 will do.

The material story replaces the category's dashboard. There are no rounded cards on a dark page, no blue accent, no gamer RGB, and the brand's paper-collage art (butter yellow, cream, graphite card) stays in the logo and the brand kit. Color is spent the way a custom keyboard spends an accent keycap: one amber key per window is the thing that window exists to do; coral appears when that key becomes Stop or when something is deleted; green, orange and red exist only as lamps and message lines. Everything else is graphite, grey and off-white.

Depth is physical and has exactly three heights: recessed (wells and display glass), the plate, and raised (keycaps with a skirt and a short shadow). State is shown the way hardware shows it: a pressed key sits 1.5dp lower without its shadow, the chosen option is the light cap held down, an option that is on lights its lamp. Nothing animates; every change repaints at once.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite plate, keycaps with a visible skirt, recessed wells, black display glass.
One amber key per window; coral only to stop or delete; signal colors only as lamps and messages.
Bahnschrift (DIN) for everything printed on the hardware, Segoe UI for sentences.
Groups are silkscreen labels with a hairline, never cards.
Instant, physical state changes: travel, lamps, held-down caps; no motion.
Every metric in dp through `Theme.Dp`, every type size in points.

rules.name: The One Amber Key Rule
rules.body: Each window has exactly one amber key, the action the window exists for (Start, Run, Confirm, Apply, OK). Elsewhere amber only lights lamps and marks focus; it is never a fill, a heading color or a decoration.

rules.name: The Coral Means Stop Rule
rules.body: Coral is the key that ends what is running or deletes something. It is never a second accent and never a warning color for text; warnings are Lamp Orange.

rules.name: The Lamps Only Rule
rules.body: Green, orange and red appear only as LEDs and as the color of a message line, note or step description. They are never a key face, a fill or a border.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Bahnschrift for anything printed on the hardware (legends, labels, numbers, units, silkscreen); Segoe UI for anything that is a sentence. A number is never Segoe UI and a two-line explanation is never Bahnschrift.

rules.name: The Silkscreen Rule
rules.body: A group is named by one uppercase silkscreen label in Dim Legend, sitting low in its 28dp row and followed by a hairline. Nothing sits above it: no kicker, eyebrow or second heading.

rules.name: The Three Heights Rule
rules.body: Anything typed, listed or chosen from sits recessed; anything pressed is raised; anything live is behind glass. Nothing else gets depth.

rules.name: The Physical Press Rule
rules.body: Pressed, latched and chosen keys drop 1.5dp, show less skirt (2.5dp instead of 5.5dp) and lose their shadow. Hover lightens the face (8% toward white on graphite and grey keys, 14% on light, amber and coral keys); disabled mixes face and skirt 55% toward the plate. No glow, no scale, no animation.

dos: **Do** give each window exactly one amber key, the action it exists for (Start, Run, Confirm, Apply, OK), and make every other action a grey Mod key.
**Do** use graphite Alpha keys for options and for small or repeated actions (the number row, the step-edit bar, unchosen segments).
**Do** show the chosen option as the light cap held down inside a recessed cluster.
**Do** put everything typed in a recessed well (#111215, 7dp) whose edge turns amber (1.5dp) while it is being edited.
**Do** put live numbers, status and messages on display glass (#0B0C0E in an 11dp bezel), with a lamp for state.
**Do** open every group with a silkscreen label (8pt Bahnschrift SemiBold, uppercase, 1.4dp tracking, #A3A19A) and a hairline (#2D2F35).
**Do** draw every icon in `Icons.cs` on the 16-unit grid with one round-capped stroke.
**Do** route every pixel metric through `Theme.Dp`/`Pad`/`Sz` and give every font size in points.
**Do** keep keyboard operation, a visible amber focus mark and an accessible name and role on every painted control.
donts: **Don't** put a second amber key in a window or use amber as a fill, text color or decoration.
**Don't** use coral for anything but stopping or deleting, or green, orange and red for anything but lamps and message text.
**Don't** raise a group onto a filled, bordered card; groups live on the plate under a silkscreen label, and a hairline frame is only for a region that scrolls.
**Don't** put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading.
**Don't** use font glyphs or emoji as icons; they render differently on every Windows build and never match the legends.
**Don't** set a legend, label or number in Segoe UI, or a sentence in Bahnschrift.
**Don't** use a blue accent, RGB lighting effects or the brand kit's paper textures and collage art in the interface (the logo appears as itself, in the header).
**Don't** animate state changes or float panels on drop shadows; depth comes only from the three heights.
**Don't** set text below Dim Legend's contrast (#A3A19A, WCAG AA on the plate and on key faces).
